questions.q: The principle of keratometry is that the anterior surface of the cornea acts as a ___.
questions.exp: Keratometry principle: anterior surface of cornea acts as a convex mirror. (Book p172)

questions.q: In keratometry, the size of the image is ___ the curvature, and the image is seen as ___.
questions.exp: Size of image is proportional to 1/curvature; image seen as keratometric mires. (Book p172)

questions.q: The two photographs at the top right of the keratometry page are captioned:
opts: Keratometer and Reflection of placido disc
Keratometric mires and Good fit of lens
questions.exp: Photograph captions: Keratometer; Keratometric mires. (Book p172)

questions.q: In the diagram of correct positioning of mires, the mires must show which appearance?
opts: A single, overlapped plus sign and a single, overlapped minus sign
Two separate plus signs and a single minus sign
A single plus sign with two separate minus signs
Two separate plus signs and two separate minus signs
questions.exp: Correct positioning of mires: single, overlapped minus sign and single, overlapped plus sign. (Book p172)

questions.q: Which corneal parameter is measured by keratometry, as the first use listed?
opts: Topographic elevation of the posterior surface
questions.exp: Uses of keratometry: 1. Measure corneal curvature. (Book p172)

questions.q: Match the keratometric mire shape with the astigmatism it diagnoses — 1) Horizontally oval mires  2) Vertically oval mires  … A) Against the rule astigmatism  B) With the rule astigmatism
questions.exp: Horizontally oval mires: with the rule astigmatism. Vertically oval mires: against the rule astigmatism. (Book p172)

questions.q: For which purpose, other than measuring curvature and diagnosing astigmatism, is a keratometer used per the book?
opts: To visualise an ulcer against healthy tissue
To ascertain proper fitting of contact lens
questions.exp: Uses 3: To ascertain proper fitting of contact lens. (Book p172)

questions.q: On keratometry the mires appear pulsating. Which corneal disorder does the book say this diagnoses?
opts: Steep fit of a contact lens
questions.exp: Uses 4: To diagnose keratoconus (pulsating mires seen). (Book p172)

questions.q: In the pair of mire pictures, the one with a distorted, wavy mire circle is captioned:
questions.exp: The two mire pictures are captioned Good fit of lens (regular circle) and Steep fit of lens (wavy circle). (Book p172)

questions.q: Pachymetry measures corneal ___.
questions.exp: Pachymetry: measures corneal thickness. (Book p172)

questions.q: The normal corneal thickness (CT) in the book is:
questions.exp: Normal Corneal Thickness (CT): 0.5 to 0.6 mm (0.54 mm) or 540 micron. (Book p172)

questions.q: True or false — 'Corneal thickness is highest at the periphery and reduces towards the centre.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - CT is highest at the periphery
False - CT is uniform across the cornea
True - CT is lowest in the centre and highest at the limbus
False - CT is highest in the centre and reduces towards the periphery
questions.exp: CT is highest in the centre -> reduces towards periphery. (Book p172)

questions.q: A patient is being assessed for eligibility for LASIK, and the surgeon needs to know the corneal thickness. Which investigation does the book list for this use?
questions.exp: Pachymetry uses: 1. Eligibility for LASIK. (Book p172)

questions.q: LASIK is contraindicated if the corneal thickness is less than:
questions.exp: Eligibility for LASIK: c/i if CT < 450 micron. (Book p173)

questions.q: For IOP measurement, 1 mm Hg of IOP corresponds to how much corneal thickness?
questions.exp: IOP measurement: 1 mm Hg IOP = 10 micron of CT. (Book p173)

questions.q: Match the corneal thickness change with its effect on the measured IOP — 1) CT increased  2) CT decreased  … A) False low IOP  B) False high IOP
questions.exp: CT up -> false high IOP; CT down -> false low IOP. (Book p173)

questions.q: The colour-coded corneal thickness map and section at the top right of p173 is captioned:
questions.exp: Figure caption: Pachymetry. (Book p173)

questions.q: Corneal topography is the examination of the corneal ___.
questions.exp: Corneal topography: Examination of corneal surface. (Book p173)

questions.q: The placido disc figure is labelled with which structures?
opts: Viewing aperture with lens, keratometric mires and handle
Slit beam, reflection rings and handle
Viewing aperture with lens, reflection rings and handle
Viewing aperture with lens, reflection rings and filament
questions.exp: Placido disc labels: viewing apperture with lens, reflection rings, handle. (Book p173)

questions.q: In the figure 'Reflection of placido disc: Normal', the reflection on the cornea appears as:
questions.exp: The normal reflection of the placido disc shows regular concentric rings. (Book p173)

questions.q: Orbscan uses the ___ imaging principle.
questions.exp: Method 2: Orbscan: Uses slit scan imaging principle. (Book p173)

questions.q: Pentacam measures all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pentacam measures CT, corneal curvature, anterior segment imaging and topographic elevation maps of both surfaces. Corneal sensations are examined by the corneal aesthesiometer (p174). (Book p173)

questions.q: Pentacam produces topographic elevation maps of which corneal surfaces?
opts: Both the anterior and the posterior surface
questions.exp: Pentacam: d. topographic elevation maps of anterior surface; e. topographic elevation maps of posterior surface. (Book p173)

questions.q: What is corneal vital staining used for?
opts: To measure the depth of the anterior chamber
To map the elevation of the posterior corneal surface
To visualize and distinguish the ulcer from surrounding healthy tissue
questions.exp: Corneal vital staining: used to visualize and distinguish ulcer from surrounding healthy tissue. (Book p173)

questions.q: A corneal ulcer's floor/base shows staining because the epithelium is denuded. Which dye stains this area?
questions.exp: Fluorescein dye: stains area of denuded epithelium (floor/base of ulcer). (Book p173)

questions.q: Fluorescein is visualized under ___ light, which gives ___ fluorescence.
questions.exp: Visualized under cobalt blue light -> Green fluorescence. (Book p173)

questions.q: The ulcer diagram beside fluorescein dye shows the stain in which sites?
questions.exp: Diagram: Stain in -> Floor/base, Margins. (Book p173)

questions.q: Besides staining ulcers, fluorescein is used in ___ applanation tonometry.
questions.exp: Other uses (of fluorescein): Goldmann's applanation tonometry. (Book p174)

questions.q: Match the fluorescein test with its use — 1) Jones' dye disappearance test  2) Seidel's test  … A) Penetrating trauma  B) Lacrimation assessment  C) Dry eye by conjunctival staining
questions.exp: Jones' dye disappearance test: lacrimation assessment. Seidel's test (in penetrating trauma). (Book p174)

questions.q: Which dye stains devitalised/necrotic tissue at the margins of an ulcer?
questions.exp: Rose Bengal dye: stains devitalised/necrotic tissue (margins of ulcer). (Book p174)

questions.q: The disadvantage of Rose Bengal dye is that it can be ___ to healthy tissue.
questions.exp: Disadvantage: can be toxic to healthy tissue. (Book p174)

questions.q: Lissamine green stains devitalised/damaged tissue and, unlike Rose Bengal, is ___ to healthy ocular tissue.
questions.exp: Lissamine green dye: stains devitalised/damaged tissue. Advantage: non-toxic to healthy ocular tissue. (Book p174)

questions.q: Which dye is most commonly used for the diagnosis of dry eye by conjunctival staining?
questions.exp: Lissamine green - other uses: m/c used for diagnosis of dry eye by conjunctival staining. (Book p174)

questions.q: Alcian blue dye stains:
opts: Denuded epithelium of the ulcer floor
questions.exp: Alcian blue dye: stains mucin deposits and filaments. (Book p174)

questions.q: The three eye photographs on p174 (left to right) are captioned:
opts: Rose bengal stain, Lissamine green dye and Flourescein dye
Flourescein dye, Rose bengal stain and Lissamine green dye
Lissamine green dye, Flourescein dye and Rose bengal stain
Lissamine green dye, Rose bengal stain and Flourescein dye
questions.exp: Captions: Lissamine green dye, Rose bengal stain, Flourescein dye (plus 'Flourescein dye application' beside the fluorescein section). (Book p174)

questions.q: Which technique is a non-invasive method for in-vivo imaging of all layers of the living cornea?
questions.exp: Confocal microscopy: non-invasive technique for in-vivo imaging of all layers of living cornea. (Book p174)

questions.q: A clinician wants to examine corneal sensations using the pen-like instrument beside the nose diagram. What is it called?
questions.exp: Corneal aesthesiometer: examines corneal sensations. (Book p174)

questions.q: The corneal aesthesiometer is a pen-like instrument with a filament of what length?
questions.exp: Instrument: pen-like instrument with filament (6 cm long). (Book p174)

questions.q: As written in the book, the length of filament eliciting corneal sensations is proportional to corneal sensations, which are ___ anaesthesia.
questions.exp: Length of filament eliciting corneal sensations is proportional to corneal sensations, which are proportional to 1/anaesthesia. (Book p174)
